beats.care: If you dream of working or studying abroad, New Zealand now has visa routes set aside for Indians, from skilled jobs to a working holiday.
beats.what: India's free trade agreement with New Zealand came into force on 20 October. New Zealand dropped tariffs on all Indian exports.
beats.why: Both countries want to double two-way trade by 2030. India also gets new routes for its workers and students in New Zealand.

cards.body: The 5,000 skilled work visas need a job offer from an accredited employer, last up to three years, and do not lead straight to residency. New Zealand also promised Indian students at least 20 hours of work a week while studying.
India cut tariffs on about 70% of its product lines. Dairy, sugar and edible oils stay protected. New Zealand apples, kiwifruit and honey get in only in limited amounts, above a minimum price.
cards.title: what does india give in return?

cards.body: It is spread over 15 years, across farming, factories, infrastructure and startups.
cards.caption: investment New Zealand promised to help bring to India

cards.body: Indian exporters had been paying New Zealand tariffs of up to 10% on goods like clothes and shoes. From day one, every Indian product enters duty-free.

cards.q: Would you consider working in New Zealand?

opts: It adds work and study visa routes
cards.q: Why does this deal matter to young Indians, not just exporters?
cards.why: Besides trade, the deal sets aside skilled work visas, working holiday spots and longer post-study work for Indians.

cover.label: new skilled work visas for Indians in NZ

hook: New Zealand just opened *work visas* for young Indians. Who gets them?

learn.t: New Zealand will offer 1,000 working holiday visas a year to Indians aged 18 to 30, for up to 12 months.
